payload.description: Umbrella for closing the gap that a leaked cluster-stored deployer key can stand up operational routes and (today) drain existing routes. Sub-issues cover: moving ISM + warp-route ownership to the hardware wallet, gating the relayer with a curated route whitelist, and minimizing the deploy-time signer. See docs/architecture-decisions.md (deployer authorization) and docs/ops-decisions.md.
payload.title: Harden warp-route deploy authorization & deployer-key custody (SVM bridge)

payload.description:
The core deployer SKIPS the multisig-ISM ownership transfer on a stale assumption. deployer-scripts-config/deploy.sh:298-306 says "core transfer-ownership does not exist in the CLI ... Skipping", but `hyperlane-sealevel-client multisig-ism-message-id transfer-ownership --program-id <ism> <new-owner>` DOES exist (verified at the pinned monorepo sha 16c056a, client main.rs:676).

Impact: the ISM access-control owner = deployer key today. multisig-ism-message-id `SetValidatorsAndThreshold` enforces only owner-signer (processor.rs:374-376), so a leaked key can swap in attacker validators and forge messages for EVERY route on that ISM -> drain all collateral. This is the most severe residual hole.

Fix: replace the multisig_ism_message_id "Skipping" branch with a real transfer-ownership to HARDWARE_WALLET_PUBKEY, mirroring the working mailbox transfer-ownership block (deploy.sh:289-295). validator_announce has no owner / nothing owner-gated (instruction.rs = Init,Announce only) -> drop its warning, nothing to transfer. No monorepo bump needed (command present at the pin).
payload.title: Transfer multisig-ISM ownership to the hardware wallet during core deploy

payload.description:
warp-deployer-scripts-config/deploy.sh transfers only the route programs BPF upgrade authority (solana program set-upgrade-authority, deploy.sh:254-259). The Hyperlane app-level owner is never moved, and build_side (deploy.sh:62-75) sets no owner -> defaults to the deployer key.

Impact: that owner gates enroll_remote_routers / set_interchain_security_module / set_destination_gas / transfer_ownership on each route. A leaked key can re-point a routers or change an existing route ISM and drain that route collateral.

Fix: after deploy + the upgrade-authority transfer, call `hyperlane-sealevel-client token transfer-ownership` (exists at pin, main.rs:346; --token-type Native|Synthetic|Collateral per side, --program-id) to move each side owner to HARDWARE_WALLET_PUBKEY. Run LAST, after all owner-gated config (enroll/set-ISM/set-dest-gas) the client does during deploy. Note: once transferred, FORCE_REDEPLOY of an EXISTING route requires the hardware wallet (Ledger) to sign owner ops - acceptable/expected.
payload.title: Transfer warp-route app-level ownership to the hardware wallet during warp deploy

payload.description:
Relayer relays EVERY message between gorchain<->solana: no whitelist set, and HYP_GASPAYMENTENFORCEMENT=[{"type":"none"}] (docker-compose-hyperlane-relayer.yml). Empty MatchingList = relay-all (relayer matching_list.rs:369-375). The mailbox is permissionless (processor.rs dispatch/process), so any deployed route is operational with ZERO operator action; the warp-UI listing is cosmetic.

HYP_WHITELIST is a built-in relayer MatchingList setting (relayer settings mod.rs:50, loaded via the HYP_ env prefix, hyperlane-base loader mod.rs:98) -> config only, no agent code.

Fix: populate HYP_WHITELIST with blessed routes recipient addresses (recipientaddress = H256 hex from each route program-ids.json), assembled in the ops layer from the CURATED git route menu (mirror the warpRoutes.yaml build path), regenerated + relayer restarted when a route is added.

CRITICAL: derive from the curated git source, NOT on-chain discovery - else a leaked-key rogue route auto-whitelists itself and the gate is void. Updating the whitelist is an ops/git-reviewed config change (NOT Ledger): that is the route-endorsement governance gate.
payload.title: Gate the relayer with HYP_WHITELIST built from the curated route menu

payload.description: publish-bridge-state.yml regex-patches deployment-derived scalars (IGP IDs, mailbox, and now HYP_WHITELIST per hyp-d9c.3) into committed specs (spec-relayer.yml/spec-gas-oracle.yml/spec-warp-ui.yml) then commits+pushes. Preferred: derive these on-the-fly from the deployer's generated/ artifacts at deploy time instead of mutating committed specs. Separate concern from hyp-d9c; raised during the authz-hardening design 2026-06-09.
payload.title: Derive prod consumer config from generated artifacts (drop committed-spec patching)

payload.description:
The ops layer (PRs #25/#30) implemented bring-up (deploy-all.yml, setup-all.yml, prepare-chains, distribute-credentials, configure-dns, publish-bridge-state, stop-all) but NONE of the operator-attended maintenance playbooks the design calls for. docs/ops-decisions.md:54-62 specifies seven composite playbooks; ops/playbooks/ contains none of them:

  kill-switch.yml      MISSING
  restore.yml          MISSING
  ism-update.yml       MISSING
  teardown.yml         MISSING
  add-validator.yml    MISSING
  remove-validator.yml MISSING
  verify-ownership.yml MISSING

Trigger: ops can now deploy N validators off validators.yaml (deploy-all.yml Validators play, ~lines 132-186) — pod + MinIO IAM + DNS — but nothing updates the on-chain multisig ISM validator set. A newly-deployed validator announces to validator-announce and writes checkpoints to MinIO, but its H160 is not in any ISM, so the relayer's ISM verification ignores its signatures. The deployment side and the on-chain side were designed as separate operator actions (docs/architecture-decisions.md:310-312); only the deployment side shipped.

All on-chain steps sign via the forked hyperlane-sealevel-client with BUILT-IN LEDGER support (--keypair usb://ledger...), run on the operator's localhost, sign+broadcast in one step (docs/ops-decisions.md:7-45). 

BLOCKED ON: validation of the Ledger-support PRs (forked sealevel-client + hyperlane fork) currently under test. Implementation should not start until that signing path is confirmed working.

Reference: the archived single-validator k8s-Job pattern in deployment/ops-archive/scripts/restore.sh + templates/restore-job.yml.j2 shows the old set-validators-and-threshold call shape (pre-Ledger, pre-ansible). Authoritative spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-29-ops-layer-redesign-and-ledger-signing-design.md. Builds on the ISM-ownership-handoff work in hyp-d9c (Ledger owns the ISM, so it can authorize set-validators-and-threshold).
payload.title: Implement operator-attended bridge maintenance ops playbooks (Ledger-signed)
ism-update.yml — set ISM (validators, threshold) per chain, Ledger-signed

payload.description: Structural gap behind hyp-81f: the deployer Job can only ever set ONE validator per chain on-chain. deployer-multisig-config/{gorchain,solana}-multisig.json.tmpl hardcode a single ${X_VALIDATOR_ADDRESS} scalar with threshold 1; the scalars come from group_vars/all.yml (ops/inventories/prod/group_vars/all.yml:58-59) and are rendered once by deploy.sh:190-218. There is no path for a multi-validator initial deployment. Decide whether the deployer should derive its multisig config from validators.yaml (same H160-resolution logic ism-update needs) so a fresh deploy and a later ism-update agree on the data source, or whether initial deploy stays single-validator and ism-update is the only multi-validator path. Coupled to hyp-81f's data-model decision.
payload.title: Make initial ISM config multi-validator (derive from validators.yaml)

payload.description: ops/playbooks/kill-switch.yml (docs/ops-decisions.md:56). Emergency halt: 'deployment stop' the agents, then set ISM validators to the null set per chain via the Ledger client (set-validators-and-threshold with the 0x0..0 sentinel, see deployment/ops-archive/scripts/*.sh for the old shape). Pairs with restore.yml. Reuses the ism-update set-validators primitive. Blocked on Ledger-client validation.
payload.title: kill-switch.yml — stop agents + null the ISM validator set per chain

payload.description: ops/playbooks/restore.yml (docs/ops-decisions.md:57). Inverse of kill-switch: set ISM validators back to the real set per chain (derived from validators.yaml) via the Ledger client, then 'deployment start' the agents. Reuses the ism-update primitive. Blocked on Ledger-client validation.
payload.title: restore.yml — restore real ISM validator set + start agents

payload.description: ops/playbooks/add-validator.yml (docs/ops-decisions.md:60). Interactive: generate spec-validator-<label>.yml + edit validators.yaml, human gate (commit/PR/merge), then distribute-credentials -> configure-dns -> minio resync -> deploy the validator via stack_deploy. On-chain ISM addition is a SEPARATE ism-update.yml run (hyp-81f) — this playbook only stands up the pod/MinIO-IAM/DNS. Mirrors the existing deploy-all.yml Validators play (lines ~132-186) but for a single new validator.
payload.title: add-validator.yml — deployment-side validator onboarding

payload.description: ops/playbooks/remove-validator.yml (docs/ops-decisions.md:61). Pre-flight: ism-update.yml (hyp-81f) must have detached the validator from the ISM first. Then: 'deployment stop' the validator -> interactive spec deletion + validators.yaml edit + commit gate -> MinIO IAM cleanup (delete the per-validator user, keep its bucket) -> remove DNS. Per-validator MinIO IAM model is in ops/roles/credentials (PR #18, 93bfba3).
payload.title: remove-validator.yml — deployment-side validator offboarding

payload.description: ops/playbooks/teardown.yml (docs/ops-decisions.md:59). Operator-attended multi-step flow: 'deployment stop' agents -> loop {claim IGP fees per chain} -> loop {close program} -> close orphan buffers -> loop {transfer SOL per wallet} -> optional key disposal. Each on-chain step signs on the Ledger. Sequencing/pauses/retry belong in the playbook, not a shell script. Blocked on Ledger-client validation.
payload.title: teardown.yml — attended bridge teardown (fees, programs, SOL, keys)

payload.description: ops/playbooks/verify-ownership.yml (docs/ops-decisions.md:62). Read-only, no signing: confirm every deployed program (mailbox, ISM, IGP, validator-announce, warp routes) is owned by the hardware-wallet address. Companion to the hyp-d9c ownership handoff. Note: hyp-405 (Extend verify-ownership to check app-level ISM/route owners) is the follow-up that broadens this once the base playbook exists — base implementation belongs here.
payload.title: verify-ownership.yml — read-only program-ownership audit

payload.body: Resolved by #34 (a7ad1a5): deployment-derived values (mailbox, IGP program-ids/accounts, relayer whitelist) now render at deploy time from generated/ via ops/roles/stack_deploy/tasks/render_spec.yml — committed specs hold placeholder tokens (__GORCHAIN_MAILBOX__, __*_IGP_*__, __RELAYER_WHITELIST__) substituted into the on-host spec, gated by spec_render_generated. publish-bridge-state.yml no longer patches specs; it commits only generated/.

Priority order: (1) WebSocket-based indexing (must land before deployment — it changes how the bridge indexes chains), (2) bridge deployment, (3) this epic. ism-update design is captured at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-10-ism-update-playbook-design.md (design-only, no code). Resume at the writing-plans step.
